spain/abona.text: A Canary Islands appellation on the southern coast of Tenerife, which gained its DO in 1996. Its rules allow still, sparkling, liqueur and overripe-grape wines from many local grapes such as Listán Blanco, Listán Negro and Negramoll.

spain/arabako-txakolina.text: A Basque Country appellation in the province of Álava, around Amurrio and Llodio, for txakoli, a thin, acidic white wine that can be naturally fizzy. It is traditionally poured from a height into the glass, like cider.

spain/binissalem.text: A Spanish appellation whose rules allow still and sparkling wine from grapes such as Manto Negro, Callet and Moll, alongside Cabernet Sauvignon, Tempranillo and Chardonnay.

spain/bizkaiko-txakolina.text: A Basque Country appellation in the province of Bizkaia, covering 82 municipalities. It makes txakoli, a thin, acidic white wine that can be naturally fizzy and is traditionally poured from a height. Hondarrabi Zuri is among the allowed grapes.

spain/canary-islands.text: Spain's island wine group, with appellations on islands such as Lanzarote, La Palma, El Hierro, La Gomera and Gran Canaria, plus Tenerife areas like Abona. Listán de Huelva and Listán Negro lead plantings at 17 percent each, then Malvasia de Lanzarote at 11 and Negramoll at 4.

spain/condado-de-huelva.text: An Andalusia appellation in the south-east of Huelva province, covering about 14,800 acres and 18 municipalities. Its wines are known as the Wines of the Discovery of America. Rules allow still and liqueur wines from Zalema, Palomino Fino, Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel.

spain/el-hierro.text: A Canary Islands appellation covering the whole of El Hierro, the smallest of the seven main islands and the westernmost. It gained its DO in 1995, and its rules allow still, sparkling, liqueur and overripe-grape wines from local grapes such as Listán Blanco and Negramoll.

spain/extremadura.text: A broad Spanish Vino de la Tierra covering every municipality in the Extremadura region, which has held this status since 1999. It is one step below the main Denominación de Origen level, and Cayetana Blanca and Tempranillo are the most planted grapes.

spain/getariako-txakolina.text: A Basque Country appellation around the fishing towns of Getaria and Zarautz on the Bay of Biscay, in Gipuzkoa. It makes txakoli, a white wine that can be naturally sparkling and is poured from a height. Hondarrabi Zuri is among its allowed grapes.

spain/gran-canaria.text: A Canary Islands appellation covering the whole island of Gran Canaria, with official status since 2009. Vines arrived at the end of the 15th century, and wine became the island's main export in the 16th century before English buyers turned to Portuguese wine.

spain/granada.text: An Andalusia appellation across 168 municipalities in Granada province, plus a Contraviesa-Alpujarras sub-zone in the mountains. It became a Vino de Calidad in 2009 and a DO in 2018. Rules allow still, sparkling and overripe-grape wines from Tempranillo, Syrah, Garnacha and others.

spain/islas-canarias.text: A Canary Islands PDO spanning many municipalities across the archipelago. Its rules allow still, quality sparkling, liqueur and overripe-grape wines from local grapes such as Listán Negro, Negramoll and Malvasía Volcánica. Listán Negro is among the most planted grapes in the islands.

spain/la-gomera.text: A Canary Islands appellation covering the whole island of La Gomera, made up of six municipalities. It has had official status since 2009. Its rules allow still, sparkling, liqueur and overripe-grape wines from local grapes such as Listán Negro and Negramoll.

spain/la-palma.text: A Canary Islands appellation covering the whole island of La Palma, with about 1,500 acres of vines on a coastal strip between 650 and 4,900 feet. It has three sub-zones: Hoyo de Mazo, Fuencaliente and Norte de la Palma. It gained its DO in 1994.

spain/lanzarote.text: A Canary Islands appellation covering the whole island of Lanzarote, with about 4,400 acres of vines. It has four sub-zones, the largest being La Geria in the south. Its rules allow grapes such as Malvasía Volcánica and Listán Negro.

spain/lebrija.text: An Andalusia appellation in Seville province, covering the municipalities of Lebrija and El Cuervo de Sevilla. It is a Vino de calidad ranking below Denominación de Origen, with a single winery as of 2019. Rules allow wine from Palomino, Moscatel and Tempranillo among others.

spain/malaga.text: An Andalusia appellation for sweet and fortified wines made mainly from Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel. Its rules allow liqueur wines and wines from raisined or overripe grapes. Its sister appellation, Sierras de Málaga, covers dry still wines.

spain/montilla-moriles.text: A southern Córdoba appellation, bounded by the Genil, Guadajoz and Guadalquivir rivers. It makes mainly sweet dessert wines using sherry-style methods: flor yeast aging and a solera system. The flor gives a dry character and almond notes, and Pedro Ximénez is among the allowed grapes.

spain/pla-i-llevant.text: A PDO on Mallorca whose name means plain and east coast. Rules allow still, semi-sparkling, sparkling and liqueur wines from local grapes like Manto Negro, Callet and Moll, as well as Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Chardonnay.

spain/ribera-del-guadiana.text: An appellation in Extremadura across the Cáceres and Badajoz provinces, named for the River Guadiana.

spain/sierras-de-malaga.text: An Andalusia appellation in Málaga province, with rules allowing still wine and wine from overripe grapes.

spain/tacoronte-acentejo.text: A Canary Islands appellation on the Anaga Peninsula in northeastern Tenerife, covering about 2,500 acres. It was the first Canary Islands region to gain DO status, in 1992, and is the largest appellation on Tenerife.

spain/valle-de-guimar.text: A Canary Islands appellation on the southeastern coast of Tenerife, covering Arafo, Candelaria and Güímar. It gained its DO in 1996, and its rules allow still, semi-sparkling and liqueur wines from local grapes such as Listán Negro and Negramoll.

spain/valle-de-la-orotava.text: A Canary Islands appellation on the northwestern coast of Tenerife, covering La Orotava, Puerto de la Cruz and Los Realejos. It gained its DO in 1995, and its rules allow still, sparkling and liqueur wines from local grapes such as Listán Blanco and Negramoll.

spain/vinos-de-madrid.text: A Spanish appellation in the southern part of the Madrid region, covering 54 municipalities in three sub-zones: Arganda, Navalcarnero and San Martín. Rules allow still and quality sparkling wine from grapes such as Garnacha, Tempranillo and Airén.

spain/ycoden-daute-isora.text: A Canary Islands appellation in western Tenerife, covering towns such as Icod de los Vinos, Garachico and Guía de Isora. It gained its DO in 1994, and its rules allow wine from grapes such as Listán Blanco, Gual, Malvasía and Listán Negro.

germany/hessische-bergstrae.text: One of Germany's smallest quality wine regions, on the northern and western slopes of the Odenwald in Hesse, with about 1,150 acres of vines. It is mostly white, led by Riesling, with Pinot Gris and Spätburgunder next. Most wine is sold locally.

germany/mittelrhein.text: A German quality wine region along the Rhine, with about 1,110 acres of vines and a higher share of white grapes than any German region except Mosel. Riesling is 68 percent of plantings. Steep slopes make the work hard, and the area under vine has shrunk since 1900.

germany/saale-unstrut.text: A German quality wine region on hill slopes around the Saale and Unstrut rivers, with about 1,690 acres of vines in 2008. Most lie in Saxony-Anhalt and a small part in Thuringia.

germany/sachsen.text: A small German quality wine region along the Elbe River from Dresden to north of Meissen, with about 1,140 acres of vines. With Saale-Unstrut, it is one of Germany's two northernmost wine regions. Müller-Thurgau and Riesling lead plantings, with Pinot Blanc next.
